headword: {勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ}

definitions.explanation: Shorthand for {勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ}の{日|ひ}, the Japanese national holiday on November 23 honoring labor, production, and citizens giving thanks to one another. Historically derived from {新嘗祭|にいなめさい}, an ancient harvest festival held by the emperor.

examples.japanese: {明日|あす}は{勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ}の{日|ひ}だ。
{勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ}の{日|ひ}は{祝日|しゅくじつ}で{会社|かいしゃ}が{休|やす}みだ。
examples.english: Labor Thanksgiving Day is a holiday, so the office is closed.

examples.japanese: {幼稚園|ようちえん}では{勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ}の{日|ひ}に{合|あ}わせて、{子供|こども}たちが{両親|りょうしん}に{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}く。
examples.english: At preschool, in time for Labor Thanksgiving Day, the children write letters to their parents.

notes:
Composed of {勤労|きんろう} (labor) + {感謝|かんしゃ} (gratitude). Usually appears in the full phrase {勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ}の{日|ひ}; on its own, {勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ} is heard mainly as a name or category label.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ}の{日|ひ}: Labor Thanksgiving Day (Nov 23)
- {勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ}の{連休|れんきゅう}: the long weekend around Labor Thanksgiving

CULTURAL NOTE:
Despite the English translation, the day is not modeled on U.S. Thanksgiving. It replaced the prewar harvest festival {新嘗祭|にいなめさい} in 1948 and is now framed as a holiday honoring work and mutual gratitude in society. Schools often have children make small gifts or letters for working family members.
